payload.reason: The evidence indicates a correlation between daytime activity and socioeconomic status (SEC), suggesting that people active during the day tend to have higher SEC and use more standard language.

claims.text: People active during the day have higher socioeconomic status compared to those active at night.
Standard language use is more prevalent during the daytime, while non-standard variants are predominant at night.
The temporal variability in language use is explained by the changing composition of active users with different socioeconomic statuses throughout the day.
